abstract: This study demonstrates that workers in occupations with high AI exposure face significantly elevated unemployment risk, with findings suggesting that aggregate job losses from AI adoption may be larger than previously estimated. The research contributes to understanding how artificial intelligence exposure relates to labor market vulnerability and employment outcomes.
keyFindings: Workers in AI-exposed occupations face significantly higher unemployment risk compared to less-exposed workers
Aggregate job losses from AI may exceed earlier estimates based on occupation-level exposure analysis
methodology: Not specified in provided excerpt. Full methodology details would be available in the complete PNAS Nexus article.
